title: Physical Activity and Exercise Prescription Algorithm in Hypertension
source_reference: Ref: (85) - Metkus TS, Baughman KL, Thompson PD. Circulation 2010; MoHFW STG Annexure 2
human_review_directive: Do not index for retrieval until human verification against page image is complete.

nodes.label: Adult with diagnosed Hypertension or high cardiovascular risk
nodes.criteria: SBP >= 140 and/or DBP >= 90 mmHg or high-normal BP

nodes.label: Pre-exercise medical screening & symptom check
nodes.check: Presence of chest discomfort, jaw pain, palpitations, syncope, dyspnea, decompensated heart failure, or ACS

nodes.label: Exercise Contraindicated / Urgent Medical Evaluation
nodes.action: Do not start exercise program; evaluate and manage cardiac condition before initiating exercise.

nodes.label: Gradual Initiation for Sedentary Patients
nodes.prescription: Start with 10 minutes of moderate activity per session; gradually increase duration and intensity to minimize musculoskeletal and cardiac risk.

nodes.label: Standard Aerobic Exercise Prescription
nodes.prescription: Moderate-intensity physical activity 30 minutes/day or >= 150 minutes/week in sessions of >= 10 mins, 4-7 days/week (brisk walking at 3-4 mph, cycling, light swimming). Expect average BP reduction of 4 mmHg SBP / 2.5 mmHg DBP.

nodes.label: Muscle Strengthening / Resistance Training
nodes.prescription: Include resistance/muscle-strengthening exercises on at least 2 days per week.

document_name: MoHFW Standard Treatment Guidelines - Hypertension (Quick Reference Guide p.44 & Background Document p.127)
title: Overall Adult Hypertension Screening, Risk Stratification & Stepwise Treatment Algorithm
source_reference: Ref: (23) - European Guidelines on CVD Prevention / MoHFW Section 7 Management Pathway
human_review_directive: Do not index for retrieval until human verification against page image is complete.

nodes.label: Confirmed Hypertension Diagnosis
nodes.criteria: SBP >= 140 and/or DBP >= 90 mmHg on >= 2 clinic visits using standardized procedure

nodes.label: Universal Lifestyle Modification
nodes.action: Salt intake < 5 g/day, low fat diet, weight control (target BMI 18.5-22.9 kg/m2), regular exercise, stop tobacco.

nodes.label: Risk & Severity Stratification
nodes.check: Is HTN Grade 1 without TOD/comorbidities (<3 risk factors) vs Grade 2/3 or with Diabetes/CKD/CAD/TOD?

nodes.label: Grade 1 Lifestyle Trial (3 Months)
nodes.check: Is BP controlled to < 140/90 mmHg after 3 months?

nodes.label: Continue Lifestyle Modification & Annual/Periodic Monitoring
nodes.action: Maintain lifestyle modifications; re-evaluate clinic BP every 3-6 months.

nodes.label: Step 1: Initial Monotherapy / Low-Dose Dual
nodes.prescription: Age < 60y: ACE inhibitor (Enalapril 2.5-5 mg) or ARB (Losartan 25-50 mg); Age >= 60y: CCB (Amlodipine 2.5-5 mg) or Thiazide (Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg). Target: < 140/90 mmHg (< 150/90 in >=80y; < 130/80 in Diabetes/CKD).

nodes.label: Evaluate Step 1 BP Target at 4-6 Weeks
Maintain Current Regimen & Follow-up
nodes.action: Monitor adherence, creatinine and electrolytes every 6 months.

nodes.label: Step 2: Dual Combination Therapy
nodes.prescription: Combine two agents from different classes: ACEi/ARB + CCB (A + C) OR ACEi/ARB + Thiazide (A + D). DO NOT combine ACEi + ARB.

nodes.label: Evaluate Step 2 BP Target at 4 Weeks
Step 3: Triple Combination Therapy
nodes.prescription: Combine three classes: ACEi/ARB + CCB + Thiazide diuretic (A + C + D). Check adherence and lifestyle.

nodes.label: Evaluate Step 3 BP Target at 4 Weeks
Step 4: Resistant Hypertension & Specialist Referral
nodes.action: Add Spironolactone (MRA 25 mg) or Beta-blocker; refer to District Hospital / Specialist for secondary HTN evaluation.

title: Formulary Drug Titration & Renal Impairment Safeguards Flowchart
source_reference: MoHFW STG Quick Reference Guide Annexure 3 Formulary Summary & Page 52 Footnote
human_review_directive: Do not index for retrieval until human verification against page image is complete.

nodes.label: Renal Function Threshold Check
nodes.check: Is Creatinine Clearance < 30 ml/min (approx serum creatinine >= 3.0 mg/dl)?

nodes.label: Thiazide Contraindication / Inefficacy Rule
nodes.rule: Avoid thiazide diuretics if creatinine clearance is < 30 ml/min, as they are ineffective. Switch to loop diuretics (Furosemide). Monitor potassium and creatinine closely when using ACEi/ARBs.
nodes.footnote_text: Renal impairment: Avoid if creatinine clearance is less than <30 ml/min (approximate serum creatinine 3 mg/dl), when they may be ineffective.

nodes.label: Standard Low-Dose Thiazide & Essential Drug Formulary
nodes.guidance: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily produces near-maximal BP reduction with minimal metabolic disturbance. Amlodipine 2.5-5 mg once daily. Enalapril 2.5-5 mg once daily.
